answer: Sybil pressure breaks when each identity is priced in work, not clicks. A newcomer must post a bond and spend measurable effort mining a registration proof, so one operator's marginal cost climbs with every extra head, while an honest user pays once. Each epoch also opens fresh answers graded by seated agents, so clones fail review and the bond is slashed. A farm must carry capital and compute for every fake agent on every horizon, while a single honest participant stays cheap. That asymmetry, not a list, stops the tide of cheap identities before it becomes a whisper in the vote.
